extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism adjudication from source text, figures, Table 5, and supplement figure captions; no numeric extraction from image-only curves was required for gate closure.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Higher-helicity V13K analogs disrupted the E. coli outer membrane in an NPN uptake assay; lower-helicity multiple-D-substitution analogs showed weaker membrane permeabilization trends.
direct_assay_types: NPN uptake outer membrane permeabilization assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure curve values are trend-level in local material; no exact numerical table is present for the NPN curves.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ONPG hydrolysis in E. coli ML-35 supports peptide-induced inner membrane permeabilization, with single-D-substitution analogs retaining stronger activity than multiple-D-substitution analogs.
direct_assay_types: ONPG beta-galactosidase inner membrane permeabilization assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure curve values are not tabulated in local material; final claim is qualitative/comparative.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Tryptophan fluorescence blue shifts and intensity changes show stronger V13K interaction with prokaryotic and cancer-mimetic LUV membranes than lower-helicity D-substituted analogs.
direct_assay_types: tryptophan fluorescence in LUV model membranes
mechanism_claims.limitations: Supplement provides fluorescence/quenching figures; primary Table 5 supplies wavelength, blue-shift, and intensity values for the LUV comparison.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AFM images of V13K-treated E. coli and HeLa cells show membrane surface disruption, including bacterial membrane damage and tumor-cell membrane/cytoskeletal disruption.
mechanism_claims.limitations: AFM evidence is morphology-based and applies directly to V13K treatment; analog-specific AFM morphology is not claimed.
